Updated Energy StatementThe development hereby approved shall be carried out according to the Energy Statement by Envision Rev. A dated June 2025, or better. Following the practical completion of the development, an updated Energy Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, reflecting the measures taken in practice in Be Lean, Be Clean and Be Green stages of the Energy hierarchy to reduce carbon emitted from the operation of a development and its services, as committed to in the design stage, and the amended New Development Carbon Compensation to be paid for the remaining emissions.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that the CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policies DMD51-54 of the Development Management Document (2014), Policy SI 2 of the New London Plan 2021 and Policies SE2-SE4 of the emerging Enfield Local Plan 2019-2041 expected to be adopted in early 2026.

Overheating ReportThe development hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Overheating Report Rev. P03 dated July 2025 and install all passive and/or active measures to prevent overheating prior to first occupation of the development. Thereafter you must retain the approved passive and/or active measures to prevent overheating and maintain them in an operational condition for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure that suitable living conditions are achieved within the development and that the buildings do not overheat, in accordance with policy SI4 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy SE1 of the emerging Enfield Local Plan 2019-2041 expected to be adopted in early 2026.

Porters Lodge DetailsPrior to any works to the Porter's Lodge (Block A1), the following information shall be submitted and approved by the local planning authority.a. A condition survey on the exterior of the building, including all windows and doorways to be retained, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Where new windows and doors are proposed, large-scale drawings (at a scale of between 1:1 and 1:20, by elevation and section) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Where replacement of existing windows and doors is required, large-scale drawings (both existing and proposed, at a scale of between 1:1 and 1:20, by elevation and section) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.b. Prior to their use, a schedule specifying all external materials (including but not limited to windows, rooflights, doors, parapets, eaves, verges, cills, lintels, rainwater goods, and roof coverings) to be used shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. This schedule may, for example, include written details of manufacturer, product name or number (if applicable) and surface colour/texture together with precedent imagery at varying scales. c. A written methodology for making good all areas affected by works shall be submitted and approved, ensuring the retention and protection of historic fabric. Works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved methodology and permanently maintained as such.d. A methodology for the repair of the historic wall piers and the gateway shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submission shall include large-scale drawings, full material specifications, and a schedule of works. e. Prior to their installation, full details of the refuse and cycle storage facilities, including the boundary treatments of the new gardens, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These details shall include their precise location, design, dimensions, and external materials/finishes, ensuring that the structures are of high quality, durable, and sympathetic to the character and appearance of Block A5 and its setting.The development shall be implemented strictly in accordance with the approved details and permanently maintained as such.Reason: To safeguard heritage assets in accordance with Policy HC1 of the London Plan.

Post-Graduate Building DetailsPrior to any works to the Post-graduate building (Block A2), the following information shall be submitted and approved by the local planning authority.a. Sample panels, measuring a minimum of 1 square metre, shall be erected on site to show the areas of new exterior walling for the toilet block infill. These panels shall indicate brick size, colour, texture, and bond, together with mortar mix, joint size, colour, and pointing profile. The sample panels shall be approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and thereafter retained on site for reference for the duration of works unless otherwise agreed in writing. b. Large-scale drawings confirming the detailed design of the cornice and the location of the band course on the infill block, together with a written methodology for the re-use of any historic fabric (where applicable) and a schedule of works, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The external materials and finishes shall accord with the approved plans and/or schedule unless otherwise agreed in writing.c. A condition survey on the exterior of the building, including all windows and doorways to be retained, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Where new windows and doors are proposed, large-scale drawings (at a scale of between 1:1 and 1:20, by elevation and section) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Where replacement of existing windows and doors is required, large-scale drawings (both existing and proposed, at a scale of between 1:1 and 1:20, by elevation and section) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.d. A schedule specifying all external materials (including but not limited to windows, rooflights, doors, parapets, eaves, verges, cills, lintels, rainwater goods, and roof coverings) to be used shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. This schedule may, for example, include written details of manufacturer, product name or number (if applicable) and surface colour/texture together with precedent imagery at varying scales. e. A written methodology for making good all areas affected by works shall be submitted and approved, ensuring the retention and protection of historic fabric. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and permanently maintained as such.  Reason: To safeguard heritage assets in accordance with Policy HC1 of the London Plan.

Clock Tower DetailsPrior to any works to the Clock Tower (Building A5), the following information shall be submitted and approved by the local planning authority. To safeguard archaeological assets in accordance with Policy HC1 of the London Plan.a. Sample panels of 1 square metre minimum shall be erected on site to show areas of new, exterior walling, including 'scarring', for the rear of ground floor, and approved in writing by the local planning authority. These panels shall indicate brick size, colour, texture and bond together with mortar mix, joint size, colour and pointing profile. Upon approval the sample panels shall be retained on site for reference for the duration of works unless otherwise agreed in writing with the local planning authority. b. Notwithstanding the approved drawings, amended large-scale drawings confirming the location of 'scarring' on the clock tower, along with a methodology and schedule of works, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The external materials and finishes shall be as indicated on the approved plans and/or schedule unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.c. A condition survey on the exterior of the building, including all windows and doorways to be retained, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Where new windows and doors are proposed, large-scale drawings (at a scale of between 1:1 and 1:20, by elevation and section) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Where replacement of existing windows and doors is required, large-scale drawings (both existing and proposed, at a scale of between 1:1 and 1:20, by elevation and section) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.d. Prior to their use, a schedule specifying all external materials (including but not limited to windows, rooflights, doors, parapets, eaves, verges, cills, lintels, rainwater goods, and roof coverings) to be used shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. This schedule may, for example, include written details of manufacturer, product name or number (if applicable) and surface colour/texture together with precedent imagery at varying scales. e. A written methodology for making good all areas affected by works shall be submitted and approved, ensuring the retention and protection of historic fabric. f. Prior to their installation, full details of the refuse and cycle storage facilities shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These details shall include their precise location, design, dimensions, and external materials/finishes, ensuring that the structures are of high quality, durable, and sympathetic to the character and appearance of Block A5 and its setting. The development shall be implemented strictly in accordance with the approved details and permanently maintained as such.Reason: To safeguard heritage assets in accordance with Policy HC1 of the London Plan.

Programme of Historic Building RecordingPrior to commencement of work to any of the locally-listed buildings, a programme of historic building recording must be secured and undertaken in accordance with a written scheme of investigation which has been submitted by the applicant, and approved by the planning authority. The applicant will submit to the local planning authority an approved historic building report (to be submitted within six months of the completion of fieldwork, unless otherwise agreed in advance with the Planning Authority in consultation with the Greater London Archaeology Advice Service). This report shall be submitted to the Greater London Historic Environment Record and Local Studies Library in accordance with their guidelines and best practice.Reason: To safeguard heritage assets in accordance with Policy HC1 of the London Plan.
